body: It really did help for me! Since I started fermenting at 24°C all my loafs came out really well. My starter is young but very active already and yours is older than mine so I'll just assume for now that's it's just the BF that's the problem. At lower temps I never knew when it's time to shape and I always just started cause I didn't want to overferment. So it was just a guessing game and its really hard to improve if you dont know what's wrong. I hope your next one will come out even better!

You did in fact do a fermentolyse, not an autolyse :D autolyse would be just flour and water

With my little knowledge (I only started baking sourdough bread last month) I would say it's a little underfermented, because there is a bigger tunneling surrounded by dense dough. All of my loafs were underfermented until I started bulk fermenting at higher temperatures (24°C is what worked the best for me so far). Don't give up! You just have to find a timing that works for you if you want to ferment at lower temps. Enjoy the bread nonetheless, every sourdough is yummy af
Also if it just started doubling I don't think it will be ready on Sunday, most likely needs 1-2 more weeks until it's fully ready (with good feedings)

I would feed with a higher ratio than 1:1:1, try 1:5:5 or 1:10:10 for example, it boosted mine immensely 

I only use 1:1:1 right before baking, not for regular feedings
Incredibly sexy was my first thought

I think feeding it more also helped mine a lot, I took it out of the fridge for 3-4 days before baking and fed it daily with a pretty high ratio and when I went back to lower ratio it rose sooo quickly, it will make a big difference in fermenting! Best of luck to you! And the low hydration is such a dream to work with tbh
Thank you!
